title: Alert phasing and synthetic heartbeats — experiment notes
body:
Summary:

This note captures running experiments to reduce pager noise and incorrectly-triggered SLO-burn alerts by combining two techniques: phased alert windows ("phasing") and synthetic heartbeats for exporter/agent coverage detection. The goal is to lower noisy transient pages while keeping the backstop semantics that guarantee we detect real degradations within the SLO window.

Why we tried this:
- Recent on-call logs (JIRA-OPS-1426) show 60% of SLO-burn alerts were due to short-lived metric gaps or exporter restarts, not real user-facing latency.
- Alerting thresholds are already tuned aggressively; we need better signal hygiene before increasing threshold slack.
- Adding full-time synthetic checks gives us an explicit measure of monitoring coverage vs relying on ad-hoc counters.

Observed symptoms (examples from Q4 2024 / Jan 2025):
- Prometheus scrape spikes when kube-proxy rolls nodes -> missing target metrics for 30–120s -> burn-rate alert triggers for a single route.
- Exporter OOMKill on a batch worker, exporter restarts with 10–30s delay, Prometheus marks metric as absent; alert fires and pages SRE.
- High-cardinality labels from a new feature caused timeouts in the remote write pipeline, partial metric drop, partially-covered SLO windows.

Core hypotheses:
1) Many pages are caused by observability coverage gaps not by actual user-facing errors. A small delay before paging (phasing) allows autonomic retry & exporter restarts to heal the signal and avoid pages.
2) Synthetic heartbeat series (low-cardinality, constant-value metrics emitted from critical components every 10s) allow us to detect coverage loss quickly and treat absent application metrics differently than absent heartbeat metrics.
3) Combining phased alerting with a secondary backstop (immediate page only when heartbeat is present but metrics are bad) preserves detection speed for real issues while reducing false pages.

Experiment plan (MVP):
1) Implement synthetic heartbeats for 3 candidate tiers: API gateway, inference-runtime-pool, and metrics agent (node-exporter wrapper). Heartbeat labels: service, region, environment. Emit via StatsD -> DogStatsD exporter (existing path).
2) Deploy heartbeat ingestion rules in a dedicated prometheus scrape job and remote write to long-term store.
3) Change the SLO burn alert rule for the chosen route to a phased alert:
   - phase: 'warning' (no page) triggers after 60s sustained burn > 100
   - phase: 'page' triggers after 180s sustained burn > 100 AND heartbeat_present == true
4) Add a backstop rule: immediate page if burn > 1000 for any 30s window (critical mass), regardless of heartbeat.
5) Run for 6 weeks, track page count, mean time to acknowledge (MTTA), mean time to mitigate (MTTM), and false-positive rate estimated via post-incident review.

PromQL snippets used in the experiment (examples):
- heartbeat_present: up{job="heartbeat", service="api-gateway", env="prod"} == 1
- route_error_rate_burn: sum(increase(route_latency_seconds_burn[1m])) by (route)
- phased warning query (pseudo): sum_over_time(burn_rate[1m]) > X  # implemented with recording rules + alerting for 60s
- page gating condition (pseudo): (burn_rate_sustained_3m > X) and (absent(heartbeat_present) == 0)

Runbook snippet (quick read for oncall):
- On page: check heartbeat dashboard (panel: heartbeat -> service -> last seen).
- If heartbeat is absent for the affected service: treat as "observability gap" — do NOT escalate to infra paging until 5m of absence unless backstop hit.
- If heartbeat present and metric burn continuing: follow standard SLO mitigation steps (traffic diversion, rollback, scaling up).

Measurement & success criteria:
- Reduce non-actionable SRE pages attributable to metric absence by 50% over baseline.
- No increase in time-to-detect for real incidents (target: <3m median from user-impact to page when heartbeat present).
- Maintain >99.9% coverage of heartbeat ingestion (i.e., <0.1% of heartbeats miss a 1m window).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Heartbeats themselves become a single point of failure (if heartbeat agent dies silently, we may suppress pages).
  - Mitigation: run heartbeats from multiple independent collectors (e.g., app sidecar + node-level agent). Use dedup keys and set heartbeat TTL to 3x emission interval.
- Risk: Phasing introduces delay for real incidents that first manifest as short metric absences before user impact becomes obvious.
  - Mitigation: backstop immediate page for burn > X large (we picked 1000 tokens/min equivalent as placeholder), and monitor user-facing synthetic checks in parallel.
- Risk: Increased alert complexity makes runbooks harder to follow.
  - Mitigation: concise oncall playbook snippet above and in the Alerting UI with links.

Edge cases discovered during rollout (notes):
- Some services with extremely sporadic traffic had heartbeats suppressed by autoscaler sleep behavior; added a "startup heartbeat" on scale-up to avoid false coverage gaps.
- Remote write retention lag caused late ingestion of heartbeat metrics into the long-term store, so dashboards need to use Prometheus local view for coverage checks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: What exact thresholds map to meaningful user impact for each route? Need to map route-level token rates to user-visible latency. (Owner: Diego)
- Q: How to handle multi-region failover scenarios where heartbeat from region A is fine but metrics are missing in region B? Propose region-aware gating (Owner: Liam).
- TODO: Add automated post-incident classifier that tags incidents as "coverage-gap" when heartbeat absent for >30s and mitigated by exporter restart (JIRA-OPS-1499).
- TODO: Add a Grafana panel that shows heartbeat uptimes vs metric absence percentages over the last 90 days. (Owner: Sofia)

Slack / comms plan for full rollout:
- Week 0: announce plan in #sre and #platform-observability; request owners for candidate routes.
- Week 1: enable heartbeat for non-critical test services; confirm ingestion and dashboards.
- Week 2–3: enable phasing for selected SLOs (observability-only alert rule change, no paging). Monitor.
- Week 4: enable gated paging (heartbeat gating) for 3 production routes; monitor pages and run manual reviews.

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally experimental. Keep config PR small and reversible. If pages drop but customer-visible errors increase, rollback immediately.

References & links:
- JIRA-OPS-1426: noisy-slo-pages-Q4-report
- confluence://observability/heartbeat-experiments (design doc + dashboards)
- github.com/redwood-inference/alerting-config/pull/87 (initial rules change)

Appendix — quick checklist for the config PR reviewer:
- [ ] heartbeat metric name documented and stable (heartbeat_up_seconds_total)
- [ ] scrape job and relabel rules added, low-cardinality labels only
- [ ] alerting rule change includes phased states with clear durations and thresholds
- [ ] backstop immediate page rule exists with a large burn threshold
- [ ] dashboard panels for heartbeat and metric-absence exist and linked in the PR

End of doc.

(Notes written by Aisha during oncall rotation; will iterate based on data from week 1 run.)
